thread_b.role: concurrent cached extent update (writer of cache_es)

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([read(cache_es), use(es1)]) from thread_a -- the cached pointer must be sampled once and not refetched/replaced between the load and the in_range() check
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@__es_find_extent_range:296 = WRITE(tree->cache_es = es1) by another reader-side lookup
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: both sides hold i_es_lock only in READ (shared) mode -- the writer updates cache_es while holding the read lock, which does NOT exclude other read-lock holders -> the shared lock establishes no serialize for this write
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic(single access / short use) broken by a concurrent write under a shared read lock -> data race (a compiler refetch of cache_es could yield a bogus in_range() check)

fix_maps_to: patch reads tree->cache_es once via READ_ONCE and writes it via WRITE_ONCE -> single-copy atomicity so es1 is stable across the in_range() check; NO change to locking (read lock kept) -> maps to atomic([read,use]) at the access-marking level
recall_risk_notes: Hardest masking risk in the batch: BOTH accesses hold i_es_lock, so a lock-mode-blind 'protected/same_lock' oracle (or LLM) would conclude they are mutually excluded and SUPPRESS the race (FN). Recall requires recognizing that a write under a read/shared lock does not serialize concurrent read-lock holders. Also benign/annotation-only and a self-race (same function on two CPUs).
